frames.label: To attach a component without breaching a tube’s wall, clamp a two-piece shaft collar around the pipe and tap the col...
frames.main_point: To attach a component without breaching a tube’s wall, clamp a two-piece shaft collar around the pipe and tap the collar to accept fasteners for the add-on part. This provides a solid external mounting approach compatible with vacuum vessels.
frames.source_quote: One way would be to clamp the outside of the pipe with a two-piece shaft collar. Properly tightened, a shaft collar will resist pretty heavy loads before it slips. You could tap the shaft collar and attach your plastic part as you normally would before attaching the collar to the pipe under vacuum.

frames.label: Clamping with a shaft collar compresses the tube and can crush a thin-walled pipe, a risk increased when the tube is...
frames.main_point: Clamping with a shaft collar compresses the tube and can crush a thin-walled pipe, a risk increased when the tube is under inward (vacuum) pressure. Check wall strength—at least roughly—before relying on a collar in such cases.
frames.source_quote: Note that a shaft collar will compress the pipe, so there is some risk of crushing the pipe, especially since it is already under inwards pressure. I doubt this will be a practical concern, but it is worth doing at least a rough check if you are using a thinner pipe wall.
